summary: Frontend-only E2E testing of the live production AYANA site (https://www.ayanabott.com + https://api.ayanabott.com) after the MongoDB->Supabase migration. Signup, OTP (dev_code), child profile, plan selection, parent creation, schedule, activation, dashboard and login/session were all exercised through a real browser. RESULT: every backend endpoint returns HTTP 200 (CSRF/cookie fix works, JSONB codec works, activation returns activated:true with parent status 'sent'), BUT the reported 'Something went wrong' bug is STILL REPRODUCIBLE in the UI. Root cause is NOT CSRF — it is the axios client `timeout: 6000` in frontend/src/lib/api.js while three production endpoints take longer than 6s (POST /payment/checkout ~7.4s, POST /schedules ~6.7s, POST /activation/activate ~16.5s, GET /circle >6s). Axios aborts the request (net::ERR_ABORTED), error.response is undefined, formatApiError(undefined) renders 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' and the wizard never advances even though the server already committed the change.

minor.issue: Consistently slow: 7494ms / 7350ms / 7352ms measured (3 consecutive calls, warm). Returns 200 {skipped:true,...}
3734ms; GET /api/parents 2784ms. General per-request latency of 2.8-3.7s suggests a new DB connection/handshake per request (asyncpg pool not warm / Railway<->Supabase cross-region).

Rate limit is keyed per phone and returned 429 'Too many OTP requests. Try again in 137 seconds.' for a brand-new user on a previously used number — expected, noted so future test runs use a unique phone.

ui_bugs.issue: timeout:6000 is lower than real production latency of /payment/checkout (7.4s), /schedules (6.7s), /activation/activate (16.5s) and /circle. Requests are aborted client-side, so the UI shows 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' even though the backend returned 200 and persisted the data. There is no retry on timeout (the response interceptor only retries on 401).

PUT /profile/child returned 200 but the follow-up POST /consent exceeded 6s, so setStep(1) never ran: the Continue button spun forever and the user stayed on 'Welcome' while the server had already moved onboarding_step to 1. Only a re-login unstuck it.

Clicking 'Choose Nitya'/'Selected' shows the exact user-reported error toast 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' and does not advance to 'Your parents'. Network shows POST /payment/checkout -> net::ERR_ABORTED (client timeout), NOT 403.

POST /parents 200 and POST /consent 200 succeed, then POST /schedules is aborted at 6s -> 'Something went wrong.' toast, parent form stays open, closeParentForm() never runs so [data-testid="step2-next"] remains disabled and the user cannot reach Activate. The parent row IS created, so retrying on a 1-parent (Nitya) plan will hit the parent-limit error or create duplicate schedules (dashboard showed '2 Active schedules' after a retry).

Not clickable-testable to success: POST /activation/activate takes 16.5s vs the 6s axios timeout, so the UI button will always toast an error while the backend actually activates and sends WhatsApp. (Verified via raw fetch: 200 activated:true, status 'sent'.)
GET /api/circle aborted at 6s on two separate loads; dashboard was still showing a full-page spinner at 9s and only rendered after ~20-30s. Care circle data can silently fail to load.

Console error: 'Failed to load module script: Expected a JavaScript-or-Wasm module script but the server responded with a MIME type of text/html' plus 'X-Frame-Options may only be set via an HTTP header, not <meta>'. Likely a stale Vercel asset hash / meta tag misuse.

integration_issues.issue: Server-side state advances while the client stays behind because every mutating call is aborted at 6s. This produces the exact three symptoms the user reported (plan-step 'Something went wrong', cannot finish onboarding, cannot activate WhatsApp) even though all backend fixes are correct.
Network timeouts/aborts are indistinguishable from server errors for the user; formatApiError(undefined) returns a generic 'Something went wrong.' with no retry affordance.

issues: Currency selector defaults to USD ($10/$19/$29) even though the child timezone/phone are India (Asia/Kolkata, +91) — INR should be pre-selected from timezone/dial code.
Step labels are hidden below sm breakpoint and the 4-segment bar gives no numeric context; low-priority.
Bare centered spinner for 20-30s with no skeleton or 'still loading' copy, caused by the slow/aborted API calls.

action_items: PRIMARY FIX: raise the axios timeout in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js (line 9, currently 6000). Use >=30000 globally, or per-request overrides (e.g. 45000 for POST /activation/activate, 20000 for /payment/checkout, /schedules, /parents, /consent).

Add automatic retry (or at least a distinct 'The server is taking longer than usual — retrying...' message + Retry button) for ECONNABORTED/timeout errors so a slow response never shows 'Something went wrong'.

Make onboarding step transitions resilient: advance the wizard on the primary call's success and treat POST /consent as fire-and-forget (or run it in parallel), so a slow consent write cannot block step 0.

Make saveParentForm idempotent/recoverable: if POST /parents succeeded but POST /schedules failed, keep the created parent id and retry only the schedule instead of leaving the form open with step2-next disabled (currently leads to duplicate schedules / parent-limit errors on retry).

Investigate backend latency: 2.8-3.7s for a trivial GET and 7.4s for a payments-disabled checkout indicate per-request DB connection setup or N+1 queries; /activation/activate at 16.5s should be made async/background with a status poll.
Consider keying the OTP rate limit per user+phone and surfacing remaining time in the UI (currently a fresh signup can be blocked by another user's earlier attempts on the same number).
critical_code_review_comments: frontend/src/lib/api.js:9 — `timeout: 6000` with the comment 'short timeout so retries recover' is the direct cause of the user-visible bug; there is no retry path for timeouts (interceptor only retries on 401), so the short timeout only converts successful 200s into fake failures.
Onboarding.js saveChild(): PUT /profile/child and POST /consent are awaited serially before setStep(1); any failure of the non-critical consent call blocks a step whose real work already succeeded.

Onboarding.js saveParentForm(): parent creation, consent and schedule creation are not transactional and there is no partial-failure recovery, so a failure after POST /parents leaves orphaned parents and a permanently disabled 'Continue to activation' button.

Onboarding.js choosePlan()/activate(): errors are surfaced only via formatApiError(e.response?.data?.detail); when e.response is undefined (timeout/network) the user gets a meaningless generic message — branch on e.code === 'ECONNABORTED'.
Positive: nicknames come back as a real JSON array (['Bangaram']) from POST/GET /api/parents and render as 'Known as: Bangaram' — the JSONB codec fix is verified working.

success_rate.frontend: 40% (signup, OTP, dashboard, login/session pass; all 4 mutating onboarding steps fail in the UI due to client timeout)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Test against the live site only (no local .env / supervisor changes; /app/frontend has no .env). Use a UNIQUE phone per run (e.g. 9 + 9 random digits) or OTP /auth/otp/send returns 429. dev_code is easiest read from the /auth/otp/send response body via page.on('response'). Selectors used: signup-name/email/phone/password/submit, child-name/child-phone/child-city/child-consent/child-otp-send/child-otp-code/child-otp-verify/step0-next, select-plan-nitya, add-parent/parent-form/parent-name/parent-relationship/parent-phone/parent-language/parent-timezone/parent-nicknames/parent-consent/save-parent/step2-next, activate-care-circle. NOTE the deployed wizard has 4 steps (Welcome=0, Your plan=1, Your parents=2, Activate=3), not the 5 described in the request. After the axios timeout fix, re-run the whole flow on a brand-new email and confirm each step advances WITHOUT needing a re-login, and that no net::ERR_ABORTED appears for /payment/checkout, /schedules, /activation/activate or /circle.
rca_of_the_issue: The Supabase migration fixes (schema drift, nullable timezone, JSONB codec, COOKIE_DOMAIN/CSRF) are all confirmed working: register/login/otp/profile/checkout/parents/schedules/activate every one returns HTTP 200 in the browser with real cookies, and CSRF token is readable (csrf_present=true). The remaining user-visible failure is purely client-side: axios is created with timeout:6000 in frontend/src/lib/api.js, while post-migration production latency measured from the browser is /payment/checkout 7.4s (7494/7350/7352ms over 3 warm calls), /schedules 6.7s, /activation/activate 16.5s, /consent 3.7s, GET /parents 2.8s, GET /circle >6s. Axios therefore aborts the fetch (net::ERR_ABORTED); error.response is undefined; Onboarding.js calls formatApiError(e.response?.data?.detail) which returns the literal 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'; setStep() is skipped so the wizard freezes even though the server committed the change. Reproduction: sign up fresh -> verify OTP -> click Continue (spins forever) -> re-login lands on 'Your plan' -> click Choose Nitya -> error toast with POST /payment/checkout aborted. Mitigation: raise the axios timeout (>=30s, longer for activation), add timeout-specific retry/messaging, and reduce backend latency.
